messages:
josh-support: @sara-ml customer on Team plan seeing repeated 429s using rwd-large-64k. They get 'quota_exceeded' and occasional 401s after a burst. Happening during a nightly job that sends ~3 concurrent reqs, ~3 req/s, each ~50k tokens in the prompt. Request id sample: 01F8A7C3.

sara-ml: Can you get a sanitized sample request + full response headers? Need token counts (input vs output), concurrency per client, and whether they're using streaming. If they can reduce to 1 concurrent request, does it stop?

josh-support: Provided sanitized curl (asked customer to attach headers):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-64k","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<~50k tokens>"}],"max_tokens":1024}'
```
Customer says they see 429 bodies like: `{\"error\":{\"type\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\",\"message\":\"too many requests\"}}` and sometimes `401` immediately after a flurry. No `X-RateLimit-*` headers visible in their client logs yet.

kevin-eng: Short explainer: we enforce per-model RPM/TPM and per-instance concurrency. Large-context models are heavier (bigger KV cache, longer attention windows) so per-request effective token-cost is higher. On shared capacity this results in lower practical concurrency and tighter TPM for rwd-large-64k vs smaller models.

kevin-eng: Troubleshooting checklist:
1) Confirm 429 body: `rate_limit_exceeded` vs `quota_exhausted`.
2) Get any `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers if present.
3) Reproduce with a single-thread loop (no parallelism) to see whether RPM/TMP thresholds hit.
4) Collect `request_id`, client IP, and exact timestamps for each failed request.

anna-sre: Note about the 401s — rapid retries after 429 can exacerbate auth token TTL races (client refresh + parallel requests). Recommend exponential backoff with jitter. Example pseudo: `{\"retry_delays_ms\": [200, 500, 1200]}` and 20% jitter. Also check their token refresh logs, they may be refreshing while a request is still inflight causing transient 401s.

josh-support: Asking customer to run two quick tests: (A) single-threaded loop at 1 req/s for 5 minutes with same payload; (B) concurrent 3 threads at 3 req/s for 2 minutes. Attach raw response headers. Also asked them to try dropping prompt -> 16k tokens and retry.

sara-ml: Workarounds while we investigate: use streaming (reduces perceived latency and can lower buffer load), shorten context (chunk + retrieval/embedding), try `rwd-medium-32k` variant, or route heavy jobs to Dedicated capacity. For retries use exponential backoff + jitter and respect `Retry-After` if returned.

kevin-eng: If they can reliably repro, escalate with Support bundle: `request_ids` list, `client_ip`, timestamps (ISO8601), sanitized request body, plan id / billing account id. With that we can check routing, token accounting, and whether per-model TPM or per-customer quota triggered. Also we'll check if long-context requests were re-routed to limited long-context pools which have stricter concurrency.

josh-support: Also noted billing could manifest as 401/403; asked for billing account id. Customer will send logs and run tests. TL;DR: likely per-model TPM/concurrency exhaustion on 64k contexts — next steps: repro single-threaded, collect headers + request ids, advise backoff, try smaller model or Dedicated.

ops-bot: Incident logged INC-2026-0423. Awaiting customer debug bundle and reproduction results.
